Q5584.L1t: Pew Research Center regularly surveys people in many countries about their attitudes toward democratic institutions and freedoms.
Q5584.L2t: The 2019 Pew survey asked respondents in several countries, Italy among them, how important a free media without government censorship is.
Q5584.L3t: Italy's result was a narrow majority rather than a large one, lower than in most of the other European countries surveyed.
Q5584.L4t: A little over half of Italians, a majority but not a large one, said free media is very important.
Q5584.L2f: The 2019 survey on media freedom was run by telephone among respondents in Italy only, with no other countries compared.
Q5584.L3f: Italy's figure was among the highest in Europe, above two-thirds of respondents but below four-fifths.
Q5584.L4f: Roughly seven in ten Italians said that free media without censorship is very important.

Q5881.L1t: In propositional logic, one-step inferences rely on rules such as modus ponens and hypothetical syllogism.
Q5881.L2t: A proposition is an immediate consequence of the premises if a single application of one inference rule to them yields it.
Q5881.L3t: No premise has ~L as an antecedent leading to the biconditional, and the one-step rules available (modus ponens, hypothetical syllogism) cannot produce a conditional with that antecedent.
Q5881.L4t: The conditional running from ~L to the biconditional cannot be reached in one step from the premises.
Q5881.L2f: An immediate consequence may be reached by chaining as many rule applications as needed, as long as it is eventually derived.
Q5881.L3f: A conditional with ~L as its consequent can be detached in one step using only the third premise, so ~L is reached without any extra step, whereas the conditional with ~L as antecedent follows from the first premise by a standard rule.
Q5881.L4f: The bare negation ~L is not an immediate one-step consequence of the premises.

Q5171.L1t: Blood transfusion requires compatibility testing and careful patient identity checks at the bedside.
Q5171.L2t: Blood products are kept under controlled refrigeration in the blood bank until they are issued for a patient.
Q5171.L3t: Once a unit warms outside controlled storage bacterial growth becomes a concern, so the allowed window before starting is far shorter than the up to 4 hours a full unit takes to infuse, and units not started in time are returned to the blood bank.
Q5171.L4t: The transfusion should begin within half an hour of the unit leaving refrigeration.
Q5171.L2f: Blood units are stored frozen at minus 20 degrees Celsius in the blood bank and thawed on request before being issued.
Q5171.L3f: Blood kept at room temperature stays safe for roughly half a day, so the window for starting a transfusion after leaving the fridge is very generous.
Q5171.L4f: A transfusion can safely begin as late as half a day after the unit leaves refrigeration.
